name: ccr
_marker_style: plain — pinned for this A/B. The CCR-off arm's omission marker recommends a grep/head re-run; both tasks below are designed so the answer is identifiable ONLY by a relational, non-greppable predicate (a checksum/framesum the model must compute over the block's contents and compare). No single grep/head/sed/PCRE on any anchor isolates it, and the discriminating block sits in the omitted middle, so the control must pull the whole output back into context to recover it. Vary the arm with --hook-arg-arms 'ccr-on=,ccr-off=--ccr off', NOT --marker-style.

tasks.prompt: Run the script with: bash run.sh  (run that command in Bash; do NOT open, cat, or read run.sh, check.sh, or any output file — work only from the command's terminal output). The output is a large diagnostic dump containing MANY blocks delimited by '=== ANALYSIS SECTION ===' / '=== END ANALYSIS SECTION ==='. Every block has exactly six 'metric: NAME=VALUE' lines (orders_total, revenue_usd, refunds_total, active_users, error_rate_ppm, p99_latency_ms) and is preceded by a header line of the form '>>> audit run=AUD-XXXXX checksum=N <<<'. All but one block are DECOYS: a decoy's six values do NOT sum to the checksum on its header (and decoy values share the same magnitude as the real ones, so neither a keyword grep nor a digit-count grep isolates the answer). Exactly ONE block is the real audited rollup: the UNIQUE block whose six metric values SUM EXACTLY to the checksum printed on its own '>>> audit ... checksum=N <<<' header. Find that one block and report ONLY its six 'metric: NAME=VALUE' lines, one per line in 'NAME=VALUE' form, by writing them to a file named metrics.txt in the current directory.

Run the script with: bash run.sh  (run that command in Bash; do NOT open, cat, or read run.sh, check.sh, or any output file — work only from the command's terminal output). The output is a large service log containing MANY crash blocks. Each crash is a header line of the form '>>> request rid=REQ-XXXXX framesum=N <<<', then the line 'FATAL unhandled exception in request handler', then five 'at <function> (file:line:col)' frames. All but one crash are DECOYS: a decoy's five frame line numbers (the ':line:' field of each frame) do NOT sum to the framesum on its header, and decoy frames are drawn from the same function-name pool as the real one, so grepping 'FATAL', 'at ', 'error', or 'retry' does NOT isolate the answer. Exactly ONE crash is the real one: the UNIQUE crash whose five frame line numbers SUM EXACTLY to the framesum printed on its own '>>> request ... framesum=N <<<' header. Find that one crash and report ONLY its five 'at <function> (file:line:col)' frames, one per line, by writing them to a file named stack.txt in the current directory.
